### Chasing the Wind
Author: Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/chasing-the-wind
Passage: Ecclesiastes 1:13-14
Points:
- Solomon used his immense wealth, peace, and intellectual freedom to explore every facet of human experience.
- His honest journal confirms that all pursuits confined to this world are ultimately empty and futile.
- Because nothing under the sun brings lasting fulfillment, real hope must come from beyond the earthly realm.
- True satisfaction is found not in visible pleasures, but in trusting Jesus Christ to rule one's life.

### Solomon the Searcher
Author: Greg Laurie
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/harvestdaily/greg-laurie-devotion-january-5-2024.html
Passage: Ecclesiastes 1:14
Points:
- Despite a godly upbringing and brilliant gifts, Solomon compromised his faith and pursued worldly indulgence.
- His phrase "under the sun" describes a horizontal life lived completely without reference to God.
- Experiencing everything earth had to offer left him with the realization that it was all like chasing the wind.
- Earthly possessions cannot satisfy the human soul, whereas a life devoted to God enjoys His blessings rightly.
